subject: How to get nice tickmark placement and labels with coord_trans(x="log", y="log")?

messages.author: 20a857807016d58a
messages.subject: How to get nice tickmark placement and labels with coord_trans(x="log", y="log")?
parts:
Dear all,

below is a minimal example of a ggplot. I am wondering how I can
adjust the axis
tickmarks and labels when using "coord_trans(x="log", y="log")". As
you can see,
the ticks and labels for the x-axis are not very nicely put [they
overlap;
there are too many large ones, no small ones]. Is it possible to get
the
ticks at 10^2, 5*10^2, 10^3, 5*10^3, 10^4, say, and with labels in
scientific
format?
I tried to work with scale_x_continuous(formatter="scientific") but
received the
error:
Error in continuous_scale(c("x", "xmin", "xmax", "xend",
"xintercept"), :
unused argument(s) (formatter = "scientific")
Is this not working anymore (http://had.co.nz/ggplot2/
scale_continuous.html)?

Cheers,

Marius

### minimal example ###

require(ggplot2)
require(reshape2)
require(plyr)

## parameters of some model
p1 <- c(20, 50, 100, 200)
p2 <- c(5, 10, 20, 50, 100)
p3 <- c("group.1","group.2","group.3","group.4","group.5")
p4 <- c(0.2, 0.5, 0.8)
## replications
N <- 1000
## lengths
l1 <- length(p1)
l2 <- length(p2)
l3 <- length(p3)
l4 <- length(p4)
## build result array containing the measurements
arr <- array(rep(NA, l1*l2*l3*l4*N), dim=c(l1, l2, l3, l4, N),
dimnames=list(
p1=p1,
p2=p2,
p3=p3,
p4=p4,
N=1:N))
## fill the result array (dummy here) with values
for(i in 1:l1){
for(j in 1:l2){
for(k in 1:l3){
for(l in 1:l4){
arr[i,j,k,l,] <- i+j+k+l+runif(N)
}
}
}
}

## create molten data
mdf <- melt(arr, formula = . ~ + p1 + p2 + p3 + p4 + N) # create
molten data frame
mdf <- mutate(mdf, p12=p1*p2) # add p1*p2

## build means (dummy function here)
mdf.mean <- dcast(mdf, p1 + p2 + p12 + p3 + p4 ~ "Value",
fun.aggregate=mean, value_var="value")
str(mdf.mean)

## plot
p <- ggplot(mdf.mean, aes(x=p12, y=Value, colour=p1)) +
geom_line(aes(group=p1)) + geom_point() +
facet_grid(p3 ~ p4, scales = "free_y") +
coord_trans(x="log", y="log") # +
scale_x_continuous(formatter="scientific") [I tried this]
p
ggsave("myplot.pdf", p)
## => the spacing of the x-axis labels is not particularly nice;
additionally,
## there should be more ticks and labels for the "smaller" values,
ideally
## in "scientific" format, maybe: 10^2, 5*10^2, 10^3, 5*10^3, 10^4
